headline: Approved window, gutter, and siding changes at 6 Harrington Court, 78 Federal Street, and 159 Federal Street; continued several others to July 15.
summary: Approved a garage replacement at 225 Loring Avenue, an addition at 21 Warren Street, and several window, gutter, and siding changes. Approved a letter of support for St. Peter's Church's accessibility variance requests. Several other applications were continued to later meetings.
decisions: Found the building at 5 Orne Square historically significant, with the motion carried.
Approved providing a letter of support for St. Peter's Church's application to MAAB, 5-0.
Approved the new window configuration for the arch top gable window at 6 Harrington Court, 5-0, with prior outstanding conditions to be fixed within 30 days of issuance.
Continued 21 Winter Street to the July 15 meeting, 6-0.
Continued 1 Pickering Street to the July 15 meeting, 6-0.
Found the existing garage at 225 Loring Avenue not preferably preserved, on condition it be replaced with a garage as presented with 6 over 1 windows, 5-0 with one abstention.
Approved the windows at 1 Broad Street Unit 11 in Bahama Brown, extending the approval to the remaining third-floor units, with half screens, 5-0.
Continued 331 Essex Street to the July 15 meeting to get a drawing or rendering, 5-0.
Continued 41 Chestnut Street to the July 15 meeting, 6-0.
Approved K- or L-style gutters at 78 Federal Street under an exceptional condition of hardship, with conditions on corners, downspouts, and paint, 4-2.
Approved Hardiplank clapboard siding at 159 Federal Street on the rear elevation, with the applicant to return with any changes to paint, 6-0.
Approved the planned addition at 21 Warren Street, except the new entry with handrail system, the driveway fence, and the chimney removal, 6-0.
Continued discussion of remaining items at 21 Warren Street to September 2, 2026, 6-0.
Supported the project at 46 Chestnut Street in concept for ZBA purposes, with further discussion of details continued to July 15, 6-0.
Continued 278 Lafayette Street to the July 15 meeting at the applicant's request.
Continued 1A Cambridge Street to the August 19 meeting, 5-0.
Approved the minutes for May 20 and June 3, 5-0.

SALEM HISTORICAL COMMISSION 
MINUTES 
July 1, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Historical Commission was held on July 1, 2026 at 6:00PM via Zoom Virtual 
Meeting.  Present were Chair Vijay Joyce, Mark Meche, Robert Peterson, Milo Martinez, Brendan 
Murray (departed early), Rebecca English (arrived late).  Staff: Patti Kelleher.  Absent: Vice Chair Kelly 
Tyler-Lewis, Emily Gonzalez, Margarida Raka-Goncalves. 
 
 
5 Orne Square 
Chase P. Wrestlington Trust applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to install vents.   
 
This application was reviewed as a minor change. No abutter objection was received and a Certificate was 
issued on June 26, 2026. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to find the building historically significant.  Ms. Raka-Goncalves seconded 
the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Meche, Murray, Raka-Goncalves, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the 
motion so carried. 
 
 
St. Peter’s Church, 24 St. Peter Street 
St. Peter’s Church requested a letter of support for MAAB Variance Request.   
 
Rev. Nathan Ives was present.  Rear entrance work was completed.  This work triggered review with the 
Massachusetts Architectural Access Board (MAAB).  Submitted 11 variance requests in a package to 
MAAB.  MAAB requested support from MHC, which suggested local endorsement from SHC.  Exterior 
building envelope work includes handicapped accessibility.  The Church requested a 10-year pause in 
completing the improvements in order to raise money to make different areas accessible.  Ms. Kelleher 
presented a slide deck from Torrey Architecture to identify areas of variance requests.  Rev. Ives said that 
permanent relief would be requested in cases of the altar and balconies which could not be made 
accessible without damaging the historic fabric. 
 
Rev. Ives said that the Disabilities Commission had already provided a letter of support.  MAAB was said 
to give historic churches a wide berth, in response to Mr. Meche’s question.  Rev. Ives noted that some of 
MAAB’s requests would require disturbing resting places onsite, which was forbidden. 
 
Members were amenable to providing a letter of support.  Ms. Kelleher provided sample letters of support 
used in similar requests. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to provide a letter of support for the Church’s application to MAAB.  Mr. 
Martinez seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, Joyce were in favor and 
the motion so carried. 
 
 
 
 
 
415 Essex Street–continued discussion
Historical Commission minutes July 1, 2026 
Page 2 of 8 
 
 
City of Salem applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for heat pump installation.  Ms. Kelleher 
arranged a meeting to discuss this item with Chair Joyce and Vice Chair Tyler-Lewis. 
 
 
6 Harrington Court–continued discussion 
 
Review of windows as installed.  Anil Mezini was present.  Chair Joyce noted the plan from previous 
meeting to remove the arch top window.  A rendering was shown of what such an alteration could look 
like.  Mr. Mezini noted that the windows should be 2 over 1 whereas the rendering showed 4 over 1.  Mr. 
Meche said that the window would not be so close up against the eaves.  Ms. Kelleher indicated that the 
arch top would be removed and a horizontal divider would be added (exterior applied muntin bars) with 
trim detail to replicate and match other windows.  Members were supportive of the updated plan on the 
arch top window. 
 
Chair Joyce asked about the decorative windows which were to have been maintained but had been 
removed.  Mr. Mezini had emailed the Commission requesting the decorative windows be permitted to 
remain as installed.  Chair Joyce did not support this request and advised the applicant to continue to 
explore options to pursue salvage or replacement options.  Chair Joyce said that the original approval had 
stipulated that the vestibule windows were to be retained.  Mr. Martinez read language from the July 2024 
Certificate that was issued that stipulated retaining the decorative lites.  Ms. Kelleher showed the 
Certificate in question, noting that Pella Reserve had been modified to Jeld Wen, the key line of which 
read “Existing decorative light fixed windows on entry portico and side addition to be replaced to match 
existing design.” 
 
Mr. Mezini felt that the City’s online permitting system did not catch the discrepancy and was at fault for 
the mixup with windows.  Chair Joyce reiterated that the language of the approval in the Certificate 
needed to be followed.  Ms. Kelleher screen-shared an advisory message sent to Mr. Mezini in January 
2025 through the portal specifically stating the conditions set forth by the Commission to preserve the 
windows.   
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to approve new window configuration for the arch top gable window as 
presented with removal of arch top and introduction of applied muntins and bars to present two 2 over 1 
simulated double hung windows at location of two casement windows; and this approval was to include 
the remaining outstanding prior conditions to be rectified within 30 days of issuance.  Mr. Peterson 
seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, Joyce were in favor and the motion 
so carried. 
 
 
21 Winter Street–continuation 
Sean Maher and Karla Cassidy applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior changes.   
 
Mr. Meche presented an applicant-supplied slideshow, showing the existing entrance canopy to be 
replaced.  The canopy would still be a hip with columns.  An elevation was also shown.  Chair Joyce said 
that the fanlight could be higher.  Chair Joyce clarified that the pilasters would align with the columns.  
Mr. Maher did not plan to replace handrails which were rotted.  Chair Joyce said a handrail would be
Historical Commission minutes July 1, 2026 
Page 3 of 8 
 
needed if the top step would be 30” above grade.  Mr. Maher took reference photos from other properties 
and a book on Federal molding.  Mr. Maher said replicating the entry porch at 22 Andrew Street was the 
goal.  Mr. Meche emphasized the need for cohesion with the neighborhood and expressed preference for a 
repair of the entryway as opposed to a full restoration.  Mr. Murray agreed with Mr. Meche to the extent 
that guidelines advise against altering buildings without evidentiary reference.  Mr. Murray also said that 
enhancements should not be denied outright.   
 
Public comment: 
 
Helen Sides, architect, 35 Broad Street, said that the fanlight should not be seen from the street.  If the 
entablature was raised above the fanlight, the proportions would be incorrect.   
 
Mr. Maher was advised to continue working on moldings and handrail details.   
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to continue the application to the July 15 meeting.  Ms. English seconded 
the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, English, Joyce were in favor and the motion 
so carried. 
 
 
1 Pickering Street–continuation 
Matthew and Ellen Marshall applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for review of gas meter as 
installed.   
 
The applicants requested a continuation. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to continue the application to July 15 meeting.  Mr. Murray seconded the 
motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, English, Joyce were in favor and the motion so 
carried. 
 
 
225 Loring Avenue–continuation 
Eric and Susan Brown applied for a Waiver of the Demolition Delay to demolish garage structure older 
than 50 years.   
 
Anthony Sporidis, contractor, noted that brackets were requested from previous garage and the roof be 
made to match the existing.  New renderings and drawings were shown of the proposed garage 
replacement.  Photos of rotted framing were shown.  A vote finding the building historically significant 
was already carried out in the previous meeting. 
 
A rendering of the proposed garage reconstruction was shown.  Mr. Sporidis said the windows would be 4 
over 1.  Ms. Brown was present.  Chair Joyce and Mr. Meche praised Mr. Sporidis’s responsiveness.  Mr. 
Sporidis said the brackets would be salvaged and reused.  Mr. Meche expressed support for waiving the 
demolition delay if the garage were rebuilt as presented.  Mr. Martinez clarified that the windows were 6 
over 1 not 4 over 1.   
 
No public comment.
Historical Commission minutes July 1, 2026 
Page 4 of 8 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to find the existing building not preferably preserved on the condition 
that it be replaced with a garage as presented, incorporating elements of existing into reconstruction; with 
6 over 1 windows.  Mr. Meche seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, 
English (abstained), Joyce were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
1 Broad Street Unit 11–continuation 
Peter Quakenbos applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to replace windows.   
 
Keith Rogers was present.  A site visit was conducted to examine proposed windows.  Mr. Peterson spoke 
in favor of the proposed replacement window, as did Mr. Meche.  Mr. Rogers said that this would only be 
for one unit for the time being.  Mr. Meche questioned if an approval in this case could be applied for 
future additional installation at the same property in units with matching windows.  Two proposed colors 
were also shown – one (bronze) matched aluminum doors and Bahama Brown matched the paint when 
unfaded.  Mr. Meche and others favored Bahama Brown.  Mr. Meche recommended including comments 
about any proposed window becoming the preferred standard for similar applications. 
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to approve the windows as submitted being done in Bahama Brown and 
that the approval also apply to the remaining units on the third floor of this building so that future 
replacement window applications may proceed through application under a minor change; windows to 
include half screens.  Mr. Meche seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, 
Joyce were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
331 Essex Street–continuation 
Curwen House LLC applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to replace fencing.   
 
Richard Pabich was present.  Chair Joyce clarified that the installed fence would be flipped around and 
the corner would be angled (so that the rough side faced 331 Essex).  An invoice was shown outlining 
work to be completed, i.e. take down and reinstall lower panels to grade as best as possible to achieve 
tapered section 4’ to 6’.  Mr. Meche said that cedar posts should be used instead of pressure-treated wood.  
Chair Joyce asked whether a photograph of the old fence existed.  Mr. Martinez showed images of the 
fence on Google Maps.  Mr. Meche noted the previous fence had three rails.  Ms. Kelleher proposed 
delivering comments provided by members to the applicant to create a plan drawing.  Mr. Martinez said 
that pyramid caps were typically not approved and proposed an uncapped or beveled out post. 
 
Public comment: 
 
A neighbor’s email requested that SHC comment on the pressure treated post. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to continue the application to the July 15 meeting to get drawing or 
rendering.  Mr. Peterson seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, Joyce were 
in favor and the motion so carried.
Historical Commission minutes July 1, 2026 
Page 5 of 8 
 
41 Chestnut Street–continuation 
Richard Jagolta applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to remove fencing and install EV charger.   
 
The applicant was not present. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to continue the application to July 15 meeting.  Ms. English seconded 
the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, English, Joyce were in favor and the motion 
so carried. 
 
 
78 Federal Street  
Justin and Sonya Williams applied for a Certificate of Hardship to install gutters and downspouts.  
 
Mr. Williams spoke to the costs of gutters in light of closing costs in purchasing the home.  Half-round 
style gutters were deemed too expensive.  The roof currently has no eaves and was becoming susceptible 
to further damage.  Ms. Kelleher showed an outline of where gutters would be installed.  Chair Joyce said 
that half rounds would be most appropriate.  Mr. Williams said that many neighboring properties had K-
style.  Mr. Meche favored mitering gutters at corners which Mr. Martinez had recommended.  Chair Joyce 
clarified that gutters would be painted to match trim, and downspouts would run along cornerboards. 
 
Ms. English clarified that more than one quote had been obtained.  Mr. Martinez asked if the K styles in 
question would be seamless.  Mr. Martinez said that L-style (aka brownstone) gutters would remove one 
corner and appear more like a wooden gutter.  Mr. Martinez showed profiles of gutters in question. 
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to approve K- or L-style gutters under an exceptional condition of 
hardship, with corners to be mitered, downspouts to run along cornerboards, and painted to match trim; 
with Mr. Martinez deputized to oversee installation.  Mr. Meche seconded the motion.  Roll Call: 
Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, English (no), Joyce (no) were in favor and the motion so carried 4-2. 
 
 
159 Federal Street 
Toni Egger applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to install Hardiplank on rear (south) elevation.   
 
Robert Taylor was present.  Three sides of the house were clapboard while the rear has deteriorated wood 
shingles.  Mr. Taylor desired to replace shingles with Hardiplank clapboards, longer lasting and 
potentially cheaper.  Ms. Kelleher noted that the rear of the property was visible from Kelleher Way, a 
public way named in the district.  Mr. Meche wanted to see the exposures of the Hardiplank match the 
front.  Mr. Taylor said that the Hardiplank would be painted to match the existing body color.  Chair 
Joyce said that smooth side out would be necessary.  Mr. Martinez called attention to the cornerboard 
piece which was partially white.  Ms. Kelleher offered the option of painting to match existing or treating 
cornerboard as trim. 
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to approve the Hardiplank clapboard siding, with same exposure 
dimension as front, smooth side out, painted to match existing body color; with applicant to return with
Historical Commission minutes July 1, 2026 
Page 6 of 8 
 
any changes to paint.  Ms. English seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, 
English, Joyce were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
21 Warren Street 
Carrie and Lee Dichter applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior modifications and 2-story 
addition.   
 
Helen Sides was present with applicants.  Ms. Sides said the project also requires zoning relief from 
Zoning Board of Appeals.  Ms. Sides said the addition would be recessed on both sides of the house.  A 
one-story porch on the rear of the house exists.  Windows for addition would be 2 over 2’s.  Ms. Sides 
also said that a chimney would be removed.  Elevations were shown, including the rear.  An image from 
Broad Street was shown.  Details for railings were shown from neighboring property at 23 Warren Street.  
Ms. Sides preferred smaller posts than those featuring at 23 Warren Street.  Ms. Sides also said that 
applicants wanted to put a 6’ fence along the driveway. 
 
Mr. Meche appreciated that the project will remove the existing exterior line sets in the rear of the 
property, as well as distinguishing addition from existing.  Ms. English questioned if the chimney was 
visible from Warren Street.  Chair Joyce said that dual chimneys were seen as a pattern at various 
addresses on Warren (e.g. 23, 14, 17, etc.).  Chair Joyce questioned if the chimney could be retained 
above the roofline.  Chair Joyce complimented other elements of the project, such as the porch which 
emulated Victorian style.  Ms. Kelleher noted that the line set featuring the rear of the property was not 
installed with approval.  Mr. Meche wondered whether it could be moved inside.  Ms. Kelleher noted 
other properties on Warren and Broad Streets that were required to retain chimneys above roofline.   
 
Public comment: 
 
A supportive email from Nick Lewis, neighbor, noted that the applicants shared plans in advance of the 
meeting. 
 
Ms. Sides strongly opposed Chair Joyce’s suggestion of retaining the chimney above the roofline and 
reinforcing it with steel.  Mr. Murray said that faux chimneys had come a long way.  Ms. Kelleher noted a 
recent case in which a chimney was removed without permission and the owner was required to 
reconstruct. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to approve the planned addition as presented, with exception of new entry 
(including handrail system), driveway fence, and chimney removal.  Mr. Peterson seconded the motion.  
Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, English, Joyce were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to continue discussion of remaining items to meeting on September 2, 
2026.  Mr. Peterson seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, English, Joyce 
were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
46 Chestnut Street 
Robert and Elizabeth Beverly applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior modifications and 
1-story addition.
Historical Commission minutes July 1, 2026 
Page 7 of 8 
 
Brian Labau, architect, was present to discuss the replacement of an existing rear deck with a new 
addition.  Mr. Labau detailed plans to replace that footprint with a one-story mudroom and breakfast room 
addition that links back to the addition of the house.  The house was built in 1870.  The one-story wing in 
the back was not original, potentially early twentieth century.  Views from Chestnut, Essex, and Flint 
Streets were shown.  Mr. Labau noted that zoning relief from the ZBA will be required. The intent is to 
make the addition feel like a porch that was infilled.  The design featured pilasters, paneled details under 
windows, casement windows, cornice details based on the existing bay window and house itself.  
Elevation details were shown.  Clapboard would be used on north elevation, pilasters would feature on 
corners.  Frosted, leaded, or stained glass would feature to let light into the mudroom. 
 
Chair Joyce called the project “well-designed.”  Views from public ways were deemed “significant” by 
Ms. Kelleher.  Mr. Meche said the addition featured a sophisticated level of detail which could be more 
modest.  Chair Joyce found the level of detailed sophistication appropriate for this particular property.  
Mr. Martinez agreed with Mr. Meche.  Mr. Meche favored pilasters over columns.  Mr. Martinez 
identified property at the corner of Warren and Flint as a potential inspiration to emulate, as a porch 
which was then enclosed.  Mr. Peterson and Ms. English were supportive of the design as submitted.  Mr. 
Meche wanted to see the addition brought down a notch in the styles it was adding to.  Mr. Murray 
enjoyed the concept and idea of the addition as presented.   
 
No public comment. 
 
Mr. Labau spoke to the need to maximize interior space in designing the addition.  Members had no 
issues with the footprint or general massing of the addition but felt further modification of details were 
needed.  Mr. Meche wanted to see the addition differentiate itself from existing.   
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to support the project in concept for ZBA purposes with further 
presentation and discussion of details continued to July 15.  Mr. Martinez seconded the motion.  Roll 
Call: Peterson, Murray, Martinez, Meche, English, Joyce were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
278 Lafayette Street 
Robert J. Willwerth applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior modifications.   
 
The applicant requested a continuation. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to continue the application to July 15 meeting.  Mr. Murray seconded the 
motion.  Roll Call: All were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
1A Cambridge Street 
Eleanor Uddo applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to install solar panels.   
 
Ethan Andersen and solar rep David Carmack were present.  Mockups of solar panel placement were 
shown, some of which would be visible from Cambridge Street.  Mr. Andersen said that installation along 
the south-facing roof was preferred.  Chair Joyce was not opposed to installation of solar panels so long as 
they were low profile and fit angles of roof.  Mr. Carmack said the solar disconnect was required by code 
so that emergency personnel or utility workers could disable the system.  The disconnect would be a blade 
level on a box similar in size to a common meter socket, which were typically installed next to the electric
Historical Commission minutes July 1, 2026 
Page 8 of 8 
 
meter and potentially required to be within 10’ of meter.  Mr. Carmack said that a design had been 
achieved which would minimize visibility of conduit.  Mr. Carmack screenshared where conduit, MSP, 
combiner, disconnect, meter (interior), and subpanel would be placed.  Mr. Carmack said that the attic and 
basement could be used to conceal conduit.  Mr. Meche advised the applicant to provide product specs, 
plans, how the panels connect to the roof, and so forth in order to carry discussion forward. 
 
No public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to continue the application to August 19 meeting.  Ms. English seconded 
the motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Martinez, Meche, English, Joyce were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
 
Other Business  
 
Minutes 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to approve minutes for May 20 and June 3.  Mr. Meche seconded the 
motion.  Roll Call: Peterson, Martinez, Meche, English, Joyce were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
 
Adjournment 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to adjourn.  Mr. Peterson seconded the motion.  All were in favor and the 
motion so carried. 
 
The meeting adjourned at 10:08PM. 
 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Dan Graham, Historic Commission Clerk
